newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs stay cool but Greenspan to weigh.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs stay cool but Greenspan to weigh.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds put on a brave face after comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Greenspan wich raised the chance of a rate hike, but traders said the impact of the statement would linger on in the next few weeks.
At 1645 GMT, the benchmark 2007 OLO was yielding 5.70 percent against 5.65 at the close on Tuesday.
"We went quite a bit lower at first but all in all the damage is modest," one trader said.
Analyst Conrad Fieremans at Kredietbank said that bonds were likely to drift further. "But from there people could be tempted to step back in, especially in the long end," he said.
Money market yields were off their highs in late afternoon but still sharply higher than on Tuesday, mainly due to a liquidity drain caused by the central bank.

The one-week repo rate was at 3.90/00 percent against 3.65/70 on Tuesday. It was still at 3.47/50 on Monday, before the bank surprised participants by cutting liquidity at its regular four-day repo operation.

Fieremans said that the central bank had tightened liquidity to support the Belgian franc, which had been trading weaker than its midpoint to the mark of 20.6255 for several weeks following domestic political scandals.
"The (central) bank has clearly chosen not to intervene in the forex market," Fieremans said.
The franc, which weakened further to more than 20.64 to the mark in morning trade, had firmed to 20.6392/00 by 1620 GMT.
Fieremens believed short-term rates would stabilise at current levels for now, but would probably edge up again in the near future.
He played down fears that a U.S. rate rise was already in the works, despite surging labour costs which could fan inflation.

Some traders said that money market rates were also pushed higher by speculation against the Dutch guilder. One said a Dutch rate hike could be expected, especially since its economy was growing stronger than in the rest of Europe.
But he added this would merely bring Dutch key rates back into line with their equivalents in the mark bloc.

The 10-year OLO/Bund yield spread, at 12 basis points on Tuesday, quickly widened to 15 early on Wednesday, but was back at 12 at the close. -- Bert Lauwers, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6815, Fax +32 2 230 7710
